marking_schemes.question_text: 'Himalayas act as a climatic divide.' Justify the statement giving two reasons.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Himalayas block the cold Siberian winds / cold winds coming from the north / coming from Siberia and also intercept / stop the monsoons forcing them to bring rains everywhere in the country. Thus towards north of Himalayas it is cold and dry and towards its south its warm and humid.
key_points: Himalayas block the cold Siberian/northern winds keeping the Indian subcontinent warm
Himalayas intercept/stop the monsoons forcing them to bring rains throughout the country, making the north of Himalayas cold and dry and south warm and humid
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Himalayas act as a climatic divide because they block the cold Siberian winds from entering the Indian subcontinent, keeping it warm. They also intercept the monsoon winds, forcing them to shed rainfall across the country, while the region north of the Himalayas remains cold and dry.
common_errors: Mentioned 'climatic divide' as the temperate zone north of Himalayas and tropical zone south of Himalayas without correct explanation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make use of wall maps while explaining the chapter on climate to enable students to understand the location of relief features and their impact on the climate.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Southwest Monsoon and Retreating Monsoon. (Any two differences)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: South West Monsoon: On-shore/sea to land; Pressure condition – low pressure over land and high pressure over sea; June – September; Advancing monsoon; Rain in most of Indian areas; periodic effects in South Asia and most of India. Retreating Monsoon: Off-shore/land to sea; Reverse pressure condition; October – November; Transition between rainy and winter; Rain in coromandel coast; October heat withdrawal of South West Monsoon affects Coromandel coast.
key_points: SW Monsoon: On-shore (sea to land); Retreating: Off-shore (land to sea)
SW Monsoon: Low pressure over land, high pressure over sea; Retreating: Reverse pressure condition
SW Monsoon: June–September; Retreating: October–November
SW Monsoon: Advancing monsoon; Retreating: Transition between rainy and winter
SW Monsoon: Rain in most of India; Retreating: Rain mainly on Coromandel coast
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Southwest Monsoon blows onshore (sea to land) from June to September, bringing rainfall to most parts of India under conditions of low pressure over land. The Retreating Monsoon blows offshore (land to sea) from October to November during a reverse pressure condition, bringing rainfall mainly to the Coromandel coast as it withdraws.
common_errors: Could give only one correct difference
Confused 'Retreating Monsoon' with 'Northeast Monsoon'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Insist on writing differences in a tabular form with corresponding points on either side. Explain clearly to students the difference between South West Monsoon and retreating monsoon.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Kolkata gets more rain than Delhi during rainy season.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bay of Bengal branch reaches Kolkata first. By the time it reaches Delhi, it is dry as it sheds the moisture on the way leaving less amount with it.
key_points: The Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon reaches Kolkata first
By the time it reaches Delhi, it has shed much of its moisture, leaving less rainfall
marking_schemes.model_answer: Kolkata gets more rain than Delhi during the rainy season because the Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon reaches Kolkata first. By the time the monsoon travels further inland to Delhi, it has already shed much of its moisture, resulting in less rainfall in Delhi.
common_errors: Failed to mention both the cities in the answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Use wall maps in class to explain geographical reasons as these cannot be explained without proper knowledge of reading a map.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Though both are hill stations, Shimla experiences snowfall during the winters but Ooty does not.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Shimla experiences snowfall in the winters and Ooty does not because Shimla is located at a much higher altitude than Ooty, in the Himalayas. Ooty is located in the Nilgiris in South India. Shimla is away from Equator and so snow line is low there whereas Ooty is closer to Equator.
key_points: Shimla is at a much higher altitude in the Himalayas, away from the Equator, so the snow line is low there
Ooty is located in the Nilgiris in South India, closer to the Equator, so temperatures do not fall low enough for snowfall
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shimla experiences snowfall during winter because it is located at a much higher altitude in the Himalayas and is farther from the Equator, resulting in a lower snow line. Ooty, situated in the Nilgiris of South India, is closer to the Equator and at a lower altitude, so temperatures do not drop sufficiently to cause snowfall.
common_errors: Failed to mention the stations in the answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give sufficient practice of reasoning-based questions to ensure that the concepts are clear.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Winter monsoons bring less rain.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Winter monsoons blow from land to sea in winter as a low pressure prevails on sea and a high pressure on land. Offshore has less moisture.
key_points: Winter monsoons blow from land to sea (offshore winds)
High pressure on land and low pressure on sea; land-originating winds carry less moisture
marking_schemes.model_answer: Winter monsoons bring less rain because they blow from land to sea (offshore direction) due to high pressure over land and low pressure over the sea. Since these winds originate over land, they carry very little moisture and therefore bring negligible rainfall.
common_errors: Instead of winter monsoon, wrote about western disturbances
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the different sources of rain in winter with the help of appropriate examples to avoid any confusion.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is Black soil found suitable for the production of cotton? (Any two points)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is moisture retentive, self-ploughing capacity, rich in minerals due to volcanic origin. Rich in carbonates of Ca and Mg. Rich in LIMCAP. Aerated. (Any two points)
key_points: Moisture retentive / self-ploughing capacity
Rich in minerals due to volcanic origin / rich in carbonates of calcium and magnesium / rich in LIMCAP / aerated
marking_schemes.model_answer: Black soil is suitable for cotton production because it is moisture retentive and has self-ploughing capacity, which helps retain water during dry spells. It is also rich in minerals such as carbonates of calcium and magnesium due to its volcanic origin, providing essential nutrients for cotton growth.
accepted_alternatives: Rich in minerals due to volcanic origin
Rich in carbonates of Ca and Mg
common_errors: Only mentioned that black soil is fertile in nature without correct explanation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay emphasis on the characteristics of soil that makes it suitable to grow certain types of crops. Ensure more practice of application-based questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one difference between each of the following: Alluvial soil of Uttarakhand and alluvial soil of West Bengal.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Uttarakhand: coarse-grained, porous alluvial soil / old / Bangar / less fertile / darker inland. West Bengal: fine-grained, compact alluvial soil / new / Khadar / fertile / deltaic or coastal / replenished, lighter.
key_points: Uttarakhand alluvial soil is coarse-grained, porous, old (Bangar), less fertile
West Bengal alluvial soil is fine-grained, compact, new (Khadar), fertile, deltaic/coastal, replenished
marking_schemes.model_answer: Alluvial soil in Uttarakhand is coarse-grained, porous, and old (Bangar type), making it less fertile, while alluvial soil in West Bengal is fine-grained, compact, and new (Khadar type), making it fertile and regularly replenished in the deltaic region.
common_errors: Mentioned alluvial soil of Uttarakhand as more fertile than that of West Bengal
Mentioned presence of Khadar in Uttarakhand and Bhangar in West Bengal (reversed)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the difference between Khadar and Bhangar using the map of India for conceptual clarity. Emphasise that examples are not considered as differences.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one difference between each of the following: Transported soil and residual soil.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Transported: Ex situ; transported by running water and found far from their parent rock / not defined profile / formed by denudation. Residual: In-situ; found where they are formed, over the parent rocks / well defined profile / formed by weathering.
key_points: Transported soil: Ex situ, carried away from parent rock by agents like running water, no defined profile
Residual soil: In situ, formed and remains over the parent rock, has a well-defined profile
marking_schemes.model_answer: Transported soil (ex situ) is carried away from its place of origin by agents such as running water and is found far from its parent rock with no defined profile, whereas residual soil (in situ) is formed by weathering and remains over the parent rock with a well-defined profile.
common_errors: Wrote examples of residual and transported soils as differences
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to write answers in complete sentences with proper explanation along with characteristics of each soil type.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to Laterite soil: How is Laterite soil formed?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is formed by leaching of essential minerals down the soil profile leaving the top soil infertile. / alternate wet and dry season / high temperature, heavy rains / weathering of lateritic rocks / desilication
key_points: Formed by leaching of essential minerals down the soil profile leaving the topsoil infertile
Occurs under conditions of high temperature, heavy rainfall and alternate wet and dry seasons / weathering of lateritic rocks / desilication
marking_schemes.model_answer: Laterite soil is formed by the process of leaching, where heavy rainfall and high temperatures wash away essential minerals from the topsoil down the soil profile, leaving it infertile. It develops under conditions of alternate wet and dry seasons through weathering of lateritic rocks.
common_errors: Wrote only 'high temperature' or 'high rainfall' as separate points without correct explanation of leaching
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the composition and characteristics of each soil type in detail as per the scope of the syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to Laterite soil: How can Laterite soil be made productive?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Use of fertilizer and irrigation facility / addition of lime
key_points: Use of fertilizers and provision of irrigation
Addition of lime to neutralize acidity
marking_schemes.model_answer: Laterite soil can be made productive by adding fertilizers and providing irrigation facilities, as well as by adding lime to neutralize its acidic nature.
common_errors: Wrote about the crops grown in laterite soil
Incorrectly mentioned the friable nature of laterite soil without explaining what should be added
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to write answers in complete sentences with proper explanation.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to Laterite soil: Name one region where Laterite soil is found.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Summits of Western & Eastern Ghats / Rajmahal hill / Part of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Kerala, Assam, Meghalaya, Goa.
key_points: Any one: Summits of Western Ghats / Eastern Ghats / Rajmahal hill / parts of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Kerala, Assam, Meghalaya, Goa
marking_schemes.model_answer: Laterite soil is found on the summits of the Western and Eastern Ghats.
common_errors: Wrote only western and eastern ghats without mentioning 'summits'
Mentioned names of states instead of regions
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the difference between region and state. Emphasise that when the question demands 'region,' writing names of states is not sufficient.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two causes of soil erosion in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Deforestation / heavy rain / faulty farming practice / shifting agriculture / overgrazing / mining / quarrying
key_points: Any two of: Deforestation / heavy rain / faulty farming practice / shifting agriculture / overgrazing / mining / quarrying
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two causes of soil erosion in India are deforestation, which removes the protective cover of vegetation, and overgrazing, which leaves the topsoil exposed and vulnerable to erosion by wind and water.
common_errors: Mentioned 'agents of soil erosion' in place of 'causes of soil erosion'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the difference between the causes and agents of soil erosion. Also, explain that causes are the reasons which lead to removal of soil.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention a soil conservation method suitable for hilly area.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Contour ploughing / Terrace cultivation / Strip cropping / crop rotation / social forestry / afforestation / dams / intercropping / cover crops / agroforestry / contour binding.
key_points: Any one of: Contour ploughing / Terrace cultivation / Strip cropping / crop rotation / social forestry / afforestation / dams / intercropping / cover crops / agroforestry / contour binding
marking_schemes.model_answer: A suitable soil conservation method for hilly areas is terrace cultivation (or contour ploughing), which reduces the speed of runoff and prevents soil from being washed downhill.
common_errors: Mentioned 'shelter belts' as method of conservation for hilly areas
Wrote conservation schemes implemented by the government instead of specific methods
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the conservation methods specific for hilly areas and make students aware of the correct terminology to describe them.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is tropical monsoon forest useful for the Indian economy? (Any two points)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: This forest has hardwood tree, the wood of which will yield durable wood for furniture / construction work / raw material for industry, paper, wax, gum, lac, raisin, honey, incense sticks, cosmetic, medicinal, livestock rearing, handicraft, perfumes, soaps, oil.
key_points: Provides durable hardwood for furniture and construction work
Provides raw materials for industries such as paper, wax, gum, lac, honey, medicinal products, perfumes, soaps, oil, etc.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical monsoon forests are useful for the Indian economy as they provide durable hardwood timber used for furniture and construction. They also yield valuable forest products such as gum, lac, honey, wax, medicinal herbs, and raw materials for industries like paper and cosmetics.
common_errors: Wrote only the characteristics of Tropical Monsoon forests instead of their economic uses
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the characteristics and uses of each vegetation belt separately and guide students to demarcate the characteristics and uses.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention the climatic condition that leads to the development of tropical desert vegetation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Temperature: 25–35°C / Scanty seasonal rain, long dry spell / less than 80% humidity. Rain: 25 cm – 100 cm / less than 50 cm
key_points: Temperature: 25–35°C / scanty seasonal rain / long dry spell / humidity less than 80%
Rainfall: 25 cm – 100 cm / less than 50 cm annually
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical desert vegetation develops under conditions of high temperatures ranging from 25–35°C with scanty seasonal rainfall (25–100 cm or less than 50 cm), long dry spells, and low humidity (less than 80%).
common_errors: Gave incorrect range of temperature and rainfall that did not match the marking scheme
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Facilitate repeated revision for learning the temperature and rainfall conditions accurately along with worksheets on a regular basis.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Mountains have varied vegetation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: In a mountain, temperature and rainfall varies with altitude / Temperature and rainfall are both high at lower altitudes and hence have denser vegetation.
key_points: Temperature and rainfall vary with altitude on mountains
Higher altitudes have lower temperature and rainfall, leading to different types of vegetation at different elevations
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mountains have varied vegetation because temperature and rainfall change with altitude. At lower altitudes, both temperature and rainfall are high, supporting dense vegetation, while at higher altitudes, conditions become colder and drier, resulting in different types of vegetation.
common_errors: Emphasised only on altitude instead of variations in temperature and rainfall
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain annual rainfall, soil distribution and temperature conditions, the growth and characteristics of vegetation belts in India using map for better conceptual clarity.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Stilt like / aerial roots are a typical feature of littoral forest.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The marshy ground of tidal forests has very compact soil that are inundated with saline water, making it difficult for roots to respire. Thus, the plants grow roots above the ground to absorb oxygen. Survive in soft and shifting mud for breathing.
key_points: The marshy, compact soil of tidal forests is inundated with saline water, making it difficult for roots to respire
Plants grow aerial/stilt roots above the ground to absorb oxygen and survive in soft, shifting mud
marking_schemes.model_answer: Aerial/stilt roots are a feature of littoral forests because the marshy ground is covered with compact soil inundated with saline water, making it impossible for underground roots to absorb oxygen. The plants therefore grow roots above the ground to respire and survive in the soft, shifting mud.
common_errors: Mentioned climatic conditions of temperature and rainfall prevalent in littoral forests instead of explaining root adaptation due to marshy land
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain in detail the meaning of the term 'littoral' forests and the specific characteristics of the natural vegetation that grows in this area along with their adaptation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason to explain each of the following: The tropical evergreen forests do not look bare at any time of the year.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Areas of tropical rain forest receive rainfall throughout the year. Hence, they do not need to shed all their leaves to conserve water during the dry season. Therefore, they never look bare / old leaves fall and new leaves grow.
key_points: Tropical evergreen forests receive rainfall throughout the year
Trees do not need to shed all leaves simultaneously; old leaves fall and new ones grow at different times, so the forest never looks bare
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical evergreen forests do not look bare at any time of the year because they receive rainfall throughout the year. Since there is no prolonged dry season, the trees do not need to shed all their leaves at once to conserve water; instead, old leaves fall and new ones grow at different times.
common_errors: Wrote that trees of the Tropical Evergreen forests never shed their leaves, instead of clarifying that shedding occurs at different times of the year
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach and highlight the basic differences between evergreen and deciduous trees.

marking_schemes.question_text: How has the rising population of India resulted in the loss of forest cover? (Any one point)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Forests converted to agricultural farms to feed the growing population. / Increased urbanization / infrastructure / Growing industrialization / mining / quarrying / Increased demand for forest products like timber
key_points: Any one of: Forests converted to agricultural farms / Increased urbanization and infrastructure / Growing industrialization, mining, quarrying / Increased demand for forest products like timber
marking_schemes.model_answer: The rising population has led to the conversion of forests into agricultural farmland to meet the increasing demand for food, resulting in significant loss of forest cover.
accepted_alternatives: Increased demand for forest products like timber
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide regular practice and clear understanding of the difference between specific methods and schemes of forest conservation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any two forest conservation methods that may be adopted to protect the forests.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Afforestation / Reforestation / Social forestry / farm forestry / agro forestry / check overgrazing / energy plantation / develop separate grazing ground / controlled grazing / Silviculture.
key_points: Any two of: Afforestation / Reforestation / Social forestry / Farm forestry / Agro forestry / Check overgrazing / Energy plantation / Develop separate grazing ground / Controlled grazing / Silviculture
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two forest conservation methods are afforestation (planting new trees in deforested areas) and social forestry (involving local communities in the planting and management of trees on non-forest land).
common_errors: Mentioned forest policy instead of 'method' for forest conservation
Mentioned only afforestation without a second method
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide regular practice and clear understanding of the difference between specific methods and schemes of forest conservation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one advantage and one disadvantage of using tank irrigation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Advantage: Simple / easy to build / subsidiary occupation - Pisciculture / Cheap / Water used for domestic purpose / help in increasing groundwater / It stores surplus rain water which could otherwise go waste. Disadvantage: They dry up when they are needed the most / dry up in summer / seasonal / Silting up of the tanks is common / problem of siltation / They occupy large area which could have been used for other productive purposes / pollution of water / loss of water by evaporation as it is shallow.
key_points: Advantage: Simple/cheap to build, stores surplus rainwater, can be used for pisciculture/domestic use/increasing groundwater
Disadvantage: Dries up in summer when needed most / silting is common / occupies large area / loss of water by evaporation / water pollution
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of tank irrigation is that it is simple and cheap to build and stores surplus rainwater that would otherwise go to waste. One disadvantage is that tanks often dry up during summer when water is needed the most, and they are prone to silting.
common_errors: Mentioned the nature of the terrain instead of highlighting the advantage
Mentioned characteristics of tank irrigation instead of its disadvantage
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain all methods of irrigation in depth so that students can write the benefits and drawbacks of each method. Explain advantage and disadvantage in a comparative tabular form.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the advantage of using Drip irrigation?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Drip irrigation conserves water as the irrigation water reaches the roots where it is needed. Reduced loss of water by evaporation.
key_points: Drip irrigation conserves water by delivering it directly to the roots
Reduces loss of water by evaporation
marking_schemes.model_answer: The advantage of drip irrigation is that it conserves water by delivering it directly to the roots of the plant where it is needed, thereby reducing water loss through evaporation.
common_errors: Mentioned the process of watering in drip irrigation instead of its advantage
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify to the students that characteristics and benefits of irrigation cannot be the same.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is Drip irrigation not practiced on a large scale in India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Expensive to develop / need of proper infrastructure / high maintenance cost / clogging of pipes.
key_points: Expensive to develop and maintain / need of proper infrastructure / clogging of pipes
marking_schemes.model_answer: Drip irrigation is not practiced on a large scale in India because it is expensive to install and maintain, requires proper infrastructure, and the pipes are prone to clogging.
common_errors: Mentioned loss of water by evaporation instead of pointing to its expensive nature or clogging of pipes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the modern methods of irrigation in detail with the help of a comparative table for better understanding.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Sprinkler irrigation is gaining popularity in recent times.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It conserves water as there is no loss of water by evaporation / even distribution. No loss of water by seepage / less water / irrigate large area / best suited for arid areas.
key_points: Conserves water as there is no loss by evaporation / ensures even distribution
No loss by seepage / can irrigate large area / best suited for arid areas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sprinkler irrigation is gaining popularity because it conserves water through even distribution with minimal loss by evaporation or seepage, and it can efficiently irrigate large areas, making it best suited for arid regions.
common_errors: Mentioned the method of Sprinkler irrigation instead of explaining why it is gaining popularity
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide more practice of reasoning questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason to explain each of the following: Tube well irrigation is used in Punjab.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Tube-well irrigation is used in Punjab because cheap hydel power is available. There is plenty of ground water and land is fertile so the cost is recovered. / soft soil easy to dig
key_points: Cheap hydel power available in Punjab
Plenty of groundwater / fertile land so cost is recovered / soft soil easy to dig
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tube well irrigation is used in Punjab because cheap hydel power is available to run the pumps, and there is an abundance of groundwater. The fertile land ensures that the cost of installation is recovered through good crop yields.
common_errors: Wrote flat area instead of high underground water table as the appropriate answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain in detail with examples which means of irrigation is available in which area and why it is available or popular in that area.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason to explain each of the following: North India has more area under canal irrigation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: In north India, there is flat land area and perennial rivers / large arable land / fertile soil / soft soil.
key_points: North India has flat land and perennial rivers
Large arable land / fertile soil / soft soil makes canal construction and irrigation feasible
marking_schemes.model_answer: North India has more area under canal irrigation because it has flat land with perennial rivers, large arable land, fertile and soft soil, making canal construction easy and irrigation efficient across vast agricultural areas.
common_errors: Wrote high underground water table instead of the presence of perennial rivers, soft soil and fertile agricultural land
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain in detail with examples which means of irrigation is available in which area and why.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the picture showing a house with rainwater being collected underground: Name the water conservation practice shown in the above picture.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Roof-top rainwater harvesting / rainwater harvesting.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Roof-top rainwater harvesting / rainwater harvesting
common_errors: Explained rainwater harvesting without mentioning the name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure maximum practice of picture related questions and answers during classroom teaching.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the picture showing rainwater harvesting: How does this system help to reduce floods?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It collects rainwater and reduces runoff and flooding.
key_points: It collects rainwater and reduces surface runoff, thereby reducing flooding
marking_schemes.model_answer: This system helps reduce floods by collecting rainwater from rooftops and channelling it into underground storage, thereby reducing surface runoff and the risk of flooding.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the importance of rainwater harvesting in the context of flood control, preventing soil erosion, etc.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the picture showing rainwater harvesting: Why is water conservation necessary? (Any two reasons)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Due to increase in population, there is a tremendous increase in demand for water. / Much water gets polluted due to faulty human activities / Much water gets wasted / Increase demand of water due to industrialization and urbanization / Reduction of underground water / Overexploitation of groundwater has lowered the groundwater table considerably / Erratic, sporadic and seasonal rain for irrigation.
key_points: Any two of: Increased demand due to rising population / Water pollution by faulty human activities / Water wastage / Increased demand due to industrialization and urbanization / Reduction of underground water / Overexploitation lowering groundwater table / Erratic and seasonal rainfall
marking_schemes.model_answer: Water conservation is necessary because the rising population has greatly increased demand for fresh water. Additionally, overexploitation of groundwater has lowered the water table considerably, making conservation essential to ensure future water availability.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the need for water conservation in the present scenario with the help of examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any three varieties of coal produced in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Anthracite / Bituminous / Lignite / Peat (Any three)
key_points: Any three of: Anthracite / Bituminous / Lignite / Peat
marking_schemes.model_answer: Three varieties of coal produced in India are Anthracite, Bituminous, and Lignite (or Peat).
common_errors: Types of iron ore such as magnetite and haematite were wrongly written as varieties of coal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make use of visual presentations such as PPT presentations to show students the different varieties of coal with their uses. Explain the varieties of coal with the help of a flow chart.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the variety of coal widely used in Iron and Steel Industries of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bituminous
marking_schemes.model_answer: Bituminous
common_errors: Identified the varieties of coal incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to write answers in tabular form to help them memorise it easily.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the state that is the largest producer of iron ore in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Odisha.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Odisha
common_errors: Most candidates were unable to identify the largest iron ore producing state correctly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to write the names of the mineral producing states and mining areas in tabular form to aid them in memorising.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any one mining area of Iron ore from the state mentioned by you (Odisha).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Gurumahishani, Badampahar, Sulaipat in Mayurbhanj district, Bonai in Sundargarh, Keonjhar. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Gurumahishani / Badampahar / Sulaipat (Mayurbhanj district) / Bonai (Sundargarh) / Keonjhar
marking_schemes.model_answer: One major iron ore mining area in Odisha is Gurumahishani (or Badampahar / Sulaipat / Bonai / Keonjhar).
common_errors: Mining area was answered wrongly due to incorrect identification of the state in 8(ii)(a)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to write the names of the mineral producing states and mining areas in tabular form to aid them in memorising.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two ways in which Hirakud dam has helped the people of Odisha.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Hirakud dam controls floods, generates power, supplies water for irrigation, canals of the dam serve as inland waterways, dam site is a popular tourist destination. Pisciculture or fishing is done in the lake behind the dam / recreation / drinking water / eradication of malaria / prevents soil erosion (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Controls floods / generates hydroelectric power / supplies water for irrigation / canals serve as inland waterways / popular tourist destination / pisciculture / recreation / drinking water / eradication of malaria / prevents soil erosion
marking_schemes.model_answer: Hirakud dam has helped the people of Odisha by controlling floods along the Mahanadi river and by generating hydroelectric power that supports industrial and domestic needs.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress on the key words while explaining topics related to multi-purpose river projects.

marking_schemes.question_text: Across which river is the Hirakud dam built?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Mahanadi.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mahanadi

marking_schemes.question_text: Give reasons for each of the following: Geothermal energy is not popular in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is confined to few areas / expensive to develop / less energy is generated / Causes air and water pollution
key_points: Confined to few areas / expensive to develop / less energy is generated / causes air and water pollution
marking_schemes.model_answer: Geothermal energy is not popular in India because it is confined to a few areas, expensive to develop, generates less energy, and can cause air and water pollution.
common_errors: Failed to understand the question and could not support answer with appropriate reasons
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress on the key words while explaining why geothermal energy is not popular, such as confined to few areas, expensive to develop, less energy generated.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give reasons for each of the following: Solar energy is gaining popularity.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: India is a tropical nation with ample sunshine / long summer / 300 sunny days / no pollution / low maintenance / inexhaustible / ecofriendly / diverse use. Subsidy by Government.
key_points: India has ample sunshine (tropical nation with ~300 sunny days) making solar energy feasible
Solar energy is non-polluting, low maintenance, inexhaustible, eco-friendly, and supported by government subsidies
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solar energy is gaining popularity because India is a tropical nation with approximately 300 sunny days per year providing ample sunshine. It is also eco-friendly, requires low maintenance, is inexhaustible, causes no pollution, and is supported by government subsidies.
accepted_alternatives: Tropical nation / ample sunshine / 300 sunny days

marking_schemes.question_text: Give reasons for each of the following: Petroleum is considered a harmful source of energy.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It causes pollution / Inflammable
key_points: Petroleum causes pollution when burned
It is inflammable, posing safety hazards
marking_schemes.model_answer: Petroleum is considered a harmful source of energy because it causes significant air pollution when burned and is highly inflammable, posing serious safety and environmental hazards.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is agriculture considered an important sector of Indian economy? (Any two points)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Major source of employment / Provides food to the large Indian population / Surplus is exported to earn foreign exchange / Provides raw materials to agro-based industries / Contributes to national income / market for industrial products / helpful for livestock rearing / earning for railways for movement of agricultural products. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Major source of employment / Provides food to large population / Earns foreign exchange through exports / Provides raw materials to agro-based industries / Contributes to national income / market for industrial products / supports livestock rearing / generates revenue for railways
marking_schemes.model_answer: Agriculture is important to the Indian economy because it is the major source of employment for a large portion of the population and provides food for India's vast population. It also earns foreign exchange through the export of surplus produce.
common_errors: Were not able to draw a relationship between agriculture and Indian economy to state its importance
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise on explaining the economic benefits of agriculture.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is mixed farming?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Growing crops and raising animals simultaneously on the same farm.
key_points: Growing crops and raising animals simultaneously on the same farm
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mixed farming refers to the practice of growing crops and raising livestock simultaneously on the same farm.
common_errors: Misunderstood mixed farming with mixed cropping
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the different types of farming clearly to students for conceptual clarity. Ensure that the meaning of important terms is grasped well by the students.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any one advantage of mixed farming.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Low wastage because agro-residue is used as animal fodder & animal dung is used as manure in the agricultural fields / Less risk for the farmer as in case of crop failure he can sustain on income from livestock farming / Higher and more steady income for the farmer. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Low wastage (agro-residue as fodder, dung as manure) / Less risk (livestock income if crops fail) / Higher and more steady income
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of mixed farming is that it reduces risk for the farmer, as in the case of crop failure, income from livestock farming can sustain the farmer.
accepted_alternatives: Less risk due to crop failure
common_errors: Since question (ii)(a) was answered incorrectly (mixing it with mixed cropping), this linked sub-part was also answered incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read the questions carefully.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: West Bengal is a leading producer of jute.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Warm average temperature of 25–35°C / humid climate (about 90% humidity) / Heavy rainfall (more than 150–200 cm annually) / Rich alluvial soil / Plenty of soft water from the Hooghly river (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Warm temperature (25–35°C) / high humidity (~90%) / heavy rainfall (150–200 cm) / rich alluvial soil / plenty of soft water from the Hooghly river
marking_schemes.model_answer: West Bengal is a leading producer of jute because it has a warm climate (25–35°C), high humidity (~90%), heavy annual rainfall (150–200 cm), and rich alluvial soil, along with an adequate supply of soft water from the Hooghly river — all of which are ideal conditions for jute cultivation.
common_errors: Mentioned the nature of jute cultivation in West Bengal instead of the physical and climatic characteristics
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the climatic characteristics for the growth of jute in West Bengal.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Millets are fast becoming the popular food crops.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: They are nutritious food crops / Cheaper option for those who cannot afford rice & wheat / Residue makes good animal fodder / Initiative by government. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Nutritious / cheaper option than rice and wheat / residue makes good animal fodder / government initiative
marking_schemes.model_answer: Millets are fast becoming popular food crops because they are highly nutritious and serve as a cheaper food option for those who cannot afford rice and wheat, while their residue also makes good animal fodder.
common_errors: Mentioned that millets require less water for growth (not in marking scheme)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide more practice of reasoning questions and instruct students to read the questions carefully.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: More than two ratoon crops are not advisable for sugarcane farmers.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Yield declines / The risk of pest infestations increases / Roots may be infected with diseases / Low sucrose content / Soil exhausting crop. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Yield declines / Risk of pest infestations increases / Roots may be infected with diseases / Low sucrose content / Soil exhausting crop
marking_schemes.model_answer: More than two ratoon crops are not advisable because the yield declines with each successive ratoon crop, the risk of pest infestations and root diseases increases, and the sucrose content of the cane decreases, making further cultivation uneconomical.
accepted_alternatives: Roots may be infected with diseases
common_errors: Wrote the definition of ratooning instead of the reason why more than two ratoon crops are not advisable
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that the meaning of important terms is understood by the students and facilitate repeated revision.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to tea cultivation, explain the term 'fine pluck'.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Plucking of two leaves and a bud which gives rise to good quality tea.
key_points: Fine pluck refers to the plucking of two leaves and a bud, which gives rise to good quality tea
marking_schemes.model_answer: Fine pluck in tea cultivation refers to the selective plucking of two leaves and a bud from the tea plant, which produces good quality tea.
common_errors: Were not able to explain the term 'fine pluck' correctly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the concept of 'fine pluck' in tea cultivation along with its benefits.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the Indian state that leads in coffee production.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Karnataka
marking_schemes.model_answer: Karnataka
common_errors: Mentioned Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh instead of Karnataka
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to remember the names of all leading states of different food crops and cash crops.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is cotton grown as a Kharif crop in India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Uniformly high temperature ranging from 21°–30°C is required during the growing period. This temperature is experienced in tropical summers. 200 frost free days / frost is harmful / rain is less likely harvest.
key_points: Cotton requires uniformly high temperature (21°–30°C) which is experienced in tropical summers
Requires 200 frost-free days; frost is harmful to cotton / rainfall is less likely during harvesting period
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cotton is grown as a Kharif crop because it requires uniformly high temperatures (21°–30°C) during the growing period, which are characteristic of tropical summers. It also needs approximately 200 frost-free days, as frost is harmful to the crop.
accepted_alternatives: Rain is less likely at harvest
common_errors: Most candidates were not able to explain why cotton is grown in the summer/kharif season
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that the meaning of the different cropping seasons is well explained in class along with the growth requirements for different crops.

marking_schemes.question_text: Based on the ownership, what type of industry is Visakhapatnam Steel Plant?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Public Sector industry
marking_schemes.model_answer: Public Sector industry
common_errors: Answered private sector instead of public sector
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss manufacturing industries with the students to help them understand the term. Clearly explain rearing and its meaning along with the production.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is meant by cooperative sector industry?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: When a group of individuals own and operate an industry collectively.
key_points: A cooperative sector industry is one where a group of individuals own and operate an industry collectively
marking_schemes.model_answer: A cooperative sector industry is one in which a group of individuals collectively own and operate an industry, sharing responsibilities and profits among members.
common_errors: Incorrectly explained that cooperative is under the government and private companies
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of how the byproducts of one industry can be used as the raw material for other industries. Facilitate regular revision to help students score better.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain the following term: Sericulture
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sericulture - The rearing of silkworms for the production of silk threads.
key_points: Sericulture is the rearing of silkworms for the production of silk threads
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sericulture refers to the rearing of silkworms for the production of silk threads.
common_errors: Incorrectly explained sericulture as production of silk (without mentioning rearing of silkworms)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain rearing and its meaning along with the production.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain the following term: Integrated steel plant
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Integrated steel plant - When all the processes of steel-making take place in one manufacturing unit.
key_points: An integrated steel plant is one where all the processes of steel-making take place within one manufacturing unit
marking_schemes.model_answer: An integrated steel plant is one in which all the processes of steel-making, from the smelting of iron ore to the final production of steel, take place within a single manufacturing unit.
common_errors: Gave vague answers without explaining that all processes happen in one unit
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of how the byproducts of one industry can be used as the raw material for other industries.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Mini-steel plants help in conservation of coal.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Mini-steel plants conserve coal as they operate on electricity and do not use coal for smelting.
key_points: Mini-steel plants operate on electricity and do not use coal for smelting, thereby conserving coal
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mini-steel plants help in the conservation of coal because they operate on electricity rather than coal for smelting, reducing coal consumption significantly.
common_errors: Wrote the meaning of mini steel plant without explaining how it helps in conservation of coal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read and practice the questions properly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: Location of sugar industry is shifting to the southern part of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Favourable climatic conditions like temperature, rainfall, frost free days ensures steady supply of sugarcane / Fertile black soil gives superior quality yields / Large land holdings / Scientific methods of farming, improved machinery / Mills located near sugarcane fields / Long crushing season / Cooperative farming / Humid climate / Sugar lobby. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Favourable climate (temperature, rainfall, frost-free days) ensures steady sugarcane supply / fertile black soil giving superior yields / large land holdings / scientific farming methods / mills near fields / long crushing season / cooperative farming / humid climate
marking_schemes.model_answer: The sugar industry is shifting to southern India because the region has favourable climatic conditions — including adequate temperature, rainfall, and frost-free days — that ensure a steady supply of high-quality sugarcane throughout the year, resulting in a longer crushing season.
common_errors: Mentioned loss of sucrose which was not required
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss with the help of a table each type of industry and the areas of availability of minerals along with other features.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one reason to explain each of the following: The electronic industry is growing at a fast rate.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: All digital devices / gadgets / Computers / Robots / Artificial Intelligence / Useful for education, defence, research, entertainment, offices, medical field, space exploration, meteorological field, postal services.
key_points: The electronic industry is growing because electronic devices are used across all sectors including education, defence, research, entertainment, medical field, space exploration, etc.
marking_schemes.model_answer: The electronic industry is growing at a fast rate because electronic devices and technologies — including computers, robots, and artificial intelligence — are now indispensable across diverse sectors such as education, defence, research, entertainment, medicine, and space exploration.
accepted_alternatives: Useful for education, defence, research, entertainment, medical field, space exploration
common_errors: Failed to explain the growth of electronic industry appropriately and gave vague answers
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss with the help of a table each type of industry for better understanding.

marking_schemes.question_text: State two conditions that favour the location of cotton textile industry in Ahmedabad.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Adequate supply of good quality raw cotton / Availability of cheap labour / Cheap hydel power from nearby area / Port facility / transport facility / Availability of capital / banking sector / humid climate / market. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Adequate supply of good quality raw cotton / cheap labour / cheap hydel power / port/transport facility / availability of capital / banking sector / humid climate / market
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two conditions favouring the location of cotton textile industry in Ahmedabad are the adequate supply of good quality raw cotton from nearby cotton-growing regions and the availability of cheap labour, along with cheap hydel power, port facilities, and access to capital.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss with the help of a table each type of industry and the areas of availability of minerals along with other features so that students are able to write their answers specifically.

marking_schemes.question_text: State any one advantage of locating Iron and Steel industry at Rourkela.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Iron ore from Mayurbhanj and Keonjhar in Odisha / Coal from Raniganj and Jharia close to it / Limestone and Dolomite from Birmitrapur Odisha / Hydroelectric power from Hirakud project in Odisha / Water from Sankh and Koel River / Manganese from Naomundi / Keonjhar. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Iron ore from Mayurbhanj and Keonjhar / Coal from Raniganj and Jharia / Limestone and Dolomite from Birmitrapur / Hydroelectric power from Hirakud project / Water from Sankh and Koel River / Manganese from Naomundi/Keonjhar
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of locating the Iron and Steel industry at Rourkela is the proximity to iron ore sources in Mayurbhanj and Keonjhar in Odisha, which reduces transportation costs significantly.
accepted_alternatives: Iron ore from Mayurbhanj and Keonjhar
Water from Sankh and Koel River
common_errors: Confused about the advantages of Rourkela location, only wrote about availability of coal, iron ore, water in general without specifying the source
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss with the help of a table each type of industry and the areas of availability of minerals along with other features so that students are able to write their answers specifically.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is road transport an important means of transport in India? (Any two reasons)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Road transport remains the most popular mode of transportation as road construction is easier and simpler / Roadways provide door to door service / Roadways are cheaper / Roadways link other modes of transport / Roadways are favourable for transporting perishable commodities / Flexible usage / Can be laid in difficult terrain / Can be used 24*7. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Road construction is easier and simpler / provides door-to-door service / cheaper / links other modes of transport / favourable for perishable goods / flexible usage / can be laid in difficult terrain / can be used 24/7
marking_schemes.model_answer: Road transport is important in India because it provides door-to-door service that no other mode of transport can offer, and it is cheaper and more flexible than other means. Roads can be laid even in difficult terrain and are usable 24 hours a day.
accepted_alternatives: Can be laid in difficult terrain
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain and clarify the basic concept in class by explaining important terms in a more elaborate manner.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Northern plain is best suited for the development of Railways.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Northern India has flat lands, softer rocks making construction easier, demand for railways is high because of high density of population, demand for movement of agricultural and industrial products is high. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Flat land makes construction easier / softer rocks / high population density creates demand / high demand for movement of agricultural and industrial products
marking_schemes.model_answer: The northern plain is best suited for railway development because it has flat land and softer rocks that make construction easier and cheaper, and its high population density creates a strong demand for railway services for both passengers and the movement of agricultural and industrial goods.
accepted_alternatives: High demand for movement of agricultural and industrial products
common_errors: Wrote about the importance of railways instead of its relation to the plains with respect to construction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the various issues related to the railways in detail with an emphasis on the role of the Central Government.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: Railways are managed completely by the Central Government.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Railways are always managed by central government as its construction involves heavy expenses that is difficult to be managed by private individuals. Moreover, railways are the principal mode of transport for both freight and passengers that needs attention and management of central government. Links several states so central government intervention is a must / influences Indian economy / defence police and army.
key_points: Railways involve heavy construction expenses that cannot be managed by private individuals
Railways are the principal mode of transport linking several states, requiring central oversight for defence, economy, and national integration
marking_schemes.model_answer: Railways are managed by the Central Government because their construction involves enormous expenses that private individuals cannot manage. Being the principal mode of transport for both passengers and freight, linking several states and playing a vital role in defence and the national economy, they require central government management.
common_errors: Could not relate the difference between state and central government with respect to management of railway
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concepts clearly to address misconceptions and common stereotypes regarding certain topics.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two advantages and one disadvantage of Inland water transport.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Advantages: Fuel efficient / environment friendly / cheapest mode of transport / most suitable for carrying bulky goods. (Any two). Disadvantage: Slowest mode of transport / dependent on weather conditions / Indian fleet is old and needs replacement / slow handling of cargo at the ports causing delay / Can be developed in only few areas. (Any one)
key_points: Advantages (any two): Fuel efficient / environment friendly / cheapest mode of transport / most suitable for bulky goods
Disadvantage (any one): Slowest mode / dependent on weather / old Indian fleet / slow cargo handling at ports / can be developed in few areas only
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two advantages of inland water transport are that it is the cheapest mode of transport and is fuel efficient and environment friendly, making it most suitable for carrying bulky goods. One disadvantage is that it is the slowest mode of transport and is dependent on weather conditions.
accepted_alternatives: Can be developed in few areas
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concepts clearly to address misconceptions and common stereotypes.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why has airway become more popular than other means of transport? (Any three reasons)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Air transport is the fastest mode of transport. Indispensable for business people, for defence, during times of emergency like epidemics, floods and earthquakes. / Air transport is gaining popularity due to private airlines offering attractive schemes and low air fare. / Drop in air fare. / Most significant in hilly and border areas which are not accessible by surface transport. (Any three)
key_points: Air transport is the fastest mode of transport, indispensable for business, defence, and emergencies
Private airlines offer attractive schemes and low air fare / drop in air fare
Most significant in hilly and border areas inaccessible by surface transport
marking_schemes.model_answer: Airways have become more popular because they are the fastest mode of transport, making them indispensable for business travellers, defence operations, and emergencies such as floods and earthquakes. The drop in air fares due to competition among private airlines has made air travel more affordable. Air transport is also the most significant means of access to hilly and border areas that are not reachable by surface transport.
accepted_alternatives: Private airlines with attractive schemes/low fares
Access to hilly and border areas
common_errors: Wrote that air transport was comfortable and safe, which was not in the marking scheme
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain and clarify the basic concepts in class.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the picture showing coloured waste bins: Which waste management method is depicted here?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Waste segregation / segregation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste segregation / segregation
common_errors: Wrongly interpreted the picture as the 3 R's (reuse, reduce and recycle)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure more practice of picture-based questions and guide students to look at pictures carefully and answer accordingly.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the picture showing coloured waste bins (waste segregation): State one way in which this method may be implemented at our home.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: We can dispose biodegradable waste like kitchen waste and non-biodegradable waste like plastic waste into separate bins.
key_points: Dispose biodegradable waste (e.g. kitchen waste) and non-biodegradable waste (e.g. plastic) into separate bins at home
marking_schemes.model_answer: At home, waste segregation can be implemented by using separate bins for biodegradable waste such as kitchen waste and non-biodegradable waste such as plastic, so each can be disposed of or recycled appropriately.
common_errors: Since 12(i)(a) was answered incorrectly, this follow-up sub-part was also answered incorrectly by those candidates
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss different methods of waste disposal and emphasise on the use of correct terminology while writing answers.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain how waste accumulation can be harmful. (Any two points)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Gaseous waste causes diseases of the lungs / Mercury poisoning cause Minamata disease / Wastes reduces the oxygen level in water (eutrophication) that kills aquatic organisms / Wastes cause biomagnification that prove toxic for the aquatic creatures / Hazardous nuclear waste / Ground water pollution by seepage from open dumps / Spoils landscape / foul smell / air/water pollution / breeding ground for flies, mosquitoes, rodents and scavengers. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Gaseous waste causes lung diseases / mercury poisoning causes Minamata disease / eutrophication kills aquatic organisms / biomagnification is toxic for aquatic creatures / nuclear waste hazard / groundwater pollution from open dumps / spoils landscape / foul smell / breeding ground for pests
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste accumulation is harmful because gaseous waste causes lung diseases and groundwater pollution through seepage from open dumps poses serious health risks. Additionally, waste accumulation can lead to eutrophication in water bodies, reducing oxygen levels and killing aquatic organisms, and creates breeding grounds for pests such as flies, mosquitoes, and rodents.
accepted_alternatives: Biomagnification is toxic for aquatic creatures
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the 'impact of waste accumulation' on the environment in detail and with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain how waste generated in the following sector may be made useful. (Give one example for each): Household
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Recycle of old newspaper, glass articles, metal scraps, plastic and converting it into useful articles. / Composting of kitchen waste. / Reusing the articles like tin boxes for storage.
key_points: Any one of: Recycling old newspaper/glass/metal scraps/plastic into useful articles / Composting kitchen waste / Reusing articles like tin boxes for storage
marking_schemes.model_answer: Household waste can be made useful by composting kitchen waste to produce organic manure, or by recycling old newspapers, glass, and metal scraps into new useful articles.
common_errors: Gave examples of domestic waste instead of highlighting the way in which it can be made useful
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide more practice of application-based questions and explain different types of waste with examples and the new products which can be made out of waste.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain how waste generated in the following sector may be made useful. (Give one example for each): Industry
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Using industrial waste like bagasse for making cardboard, molasses for alcohol / distilleries, press mud for shoe polish / carbon paper or wax / road by fly ash / fly ash as cement / bricks / scrap from steel plants used in mini steel plants.
key_points: Any one of: Bagasse for cardboard / molasses for alcohol/distilleries / press mud for shoe polish/wax / fly ash for roads/cement/bricks / steel scrap in mini steel plants
marking_schemes.model_answer: Industrial waste can be made useful by converting bagasse (sugarcane waste) into cardboard, using molasses for alcohol production, or using fly ash in the manufacture of cement and bricks.
accepted_alternatives: Steel scrap in mini steel plants
common_errors: Mentioned pollution caused by industrial waste instead of ways to repurpose and reuse it
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the reuse of various industrial waste in classroom with real life examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Explain how waste generated in the following sector may be made useful. (Give one example for each): Agriculture
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Biofuel may be made by farm waste / composting and tar making / biogas / fodder / cardboard. (One each)
key_points: Any one of: Farm waste used for biofuel production / composting / tar making / biogas / fodder / cardboard
marking_schemes.model_answer: Agricultural waste can be made useful by converting farm waste into biogas for cooking and electricity, or by composting it to produce organic manure for the fields.
common_errors: Mentioned names of agricultural waste without explaining its uses
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Facilitate revision of concept with clear understanding and explain the concept of 3 R's with examples from the agricultural sector.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two uses of composting.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Compost when added to soil makes it fertile naturally. It helps in water retention and makes soil compact / suppress plant disease / absorb odour. (Any two)
key_points: Compost makes soil fertile naturally when added to it
Helps in water retention / makes soil compact / suppresses plant disease / absorbs odour
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two uses of composting are: it makes soil fertile naturally when added to agricultural land, and it helps in water retention in the soil while suppressing plant diseases.
common_errors: Mentioned methods of composting instead of its two uses
Could mention only one use correctly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasize on the advantages and disadvantages of composting, and various waste disposal methods along with real life examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why are landfills set up far away from the city? (Any two reasons)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: To avoid spoilage of landscape / To avoid spreading of pollutants from the garbage / avoid greenhouse gas emission / Prevent health hazards and pest infestations / To avoid groundwater contamination in inhabited areas / Foul smell / Requires large area / To keep our city clean. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: To avoid spoilage of landscape / to avoid spreading pollutants/greenhouse gases / to prevent health hazards and pest infestations / to avoid groundwater contamination / foul smell / requires large area / to keep the city clean
marking_schemes.model_answer: Landfills are set up far away from the city to prevent health hazards and pest infestations within the city and to avoid groundwater contamination in inhabited areas. They are also located away from cities to prevent foul smells, spoilage of landscape, and the spread of pollutants.
accepted_alternatives: Prevent health hazards and pest infestations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the need of waste management in detail with examples.
